# When the Same Person Shows Up More Than Once

Every model so far has assumed each row is a different, independent person. This week the rows come in **clusters**: three waves from the same kid, ten days from the same sleepy participant. We'll reshape wide data to long, see why `lm()` gets the standard errors wrong when rows aren't independent, and fit our first **mixed model** with `lmer()`: random intercepts, the ICC, random slopes, and the difference between a **between-person** and a **within-person** effect.

The lecture and activity are short so that most of class is **M3 work time**.
